prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. GEAR AND PROPS sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep the same items and names. Seven tool families, each family drawn as the same mesh in three tiers left to right labelled "Copper", "Iron", "Skysteel" (same shape, only the metal colour and trim change; skysteel pale silver-blue with a faint teal edge), with the family name under each group: "Mining pick"; "Woodcutting axe"; "Herbalism sickle & satchel"; "Fishing rod & net"; "Hunting knife & snare"; "Salvage diving harness, boots & relic hook"; "Treetending tools (pruning blade, root-binding cords & moss lantern)". Top row: mining pick, woodcutting axe, herbalism sickle & satchel. Bottom row: fishing rod & net, hunting knife & snare, salvage diving harness, boots & relic hook, treetending tools. Each piece of a family stands apart from the others with a clear gap (sickle apart from satchel, rod apart from net, knife apart from snare, harness, boots and hook apart). Rods, handles and cords are thick and solid; nets and snares are solid chunky shapes with the mesh painted on. Every tool at true scale to the scale figure: a pick and an axe about 90 cm, a fishing rod about 2 m, boots knee-high. Each item alone in three-quarter front view, in rows by family or tier, with thick chunky proportions: thick blades, solid rope, chunky grips, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Skills kit: gathering tools".
